chunks: He was buried in his house, which was converted into a mosque after him according to his will, and his grave today is a well-built shrine visited for blessings in the noble Najaf.

key_terms.مَزَارٌ: shrine, place of visitation — a site frequented by pilgrims seeking blessings (tabarruk)
key_terms.مَشِيدٌ: well-built, firmly established — denotes a permanent, well-maintained structure
key_terms.وَصِيَّتِهِ: his will/testament — a legally binding final directive under Islamic law
key_terms.يُتَبَرَّكُ: blessings are sought — the practice of seeking divine grace through proximity to a pious figure's grave

ai.seo_question: Where is Sheikh al-Tusi buried and what happened to his house after his death?
ai.summary: This biographical note describes the burial of Sheikh al-Ta'ifa Muhammad ibn Hassan al-Tusi (d. 460 AH/1067 CE), the eminent Shia jurist and author of Tahdhib al-Ahkam. He was interred in his own home in Najaf; per his testament that home was later converted into a mosque, and his tomb endures to this day as a venerated shrine in Najaf al-Ashraf where the faithful seek blessings.
